name: Tolcapone
mechanism: Inhibits catechol-O-methyltransferase both peripherally and centrally, prolonging levodopa effect
dosing: Typically 100-200 mg three times daily (specialist dosing)
contraindications: History of hepatic disease or unexplained LFT abnormalities
interactions: Increases levodopa levels; interactions with other dopaminergic agents
monitoring: Liver function tests prior to initiation and regularly during treatment (risk of severe hepatotoxicity)
sideEffects: Hepatotoxicity, diarrhoea, dyskinesia, urine discoloration, orthostatic hypotension
clinicalPearls: Reserved for specialist use due to hepatic risk; requires regular LFT monitoring. Entacapone is usually preferred in routine practice.
indication: Adjunct to levodopa in Parkinson's disease with motor fluctuations (specialist use)
